summary: New box Infectum: example for sense 2 in Infectum (94/127)

data.turoyo: Bəṯr b šabṯo kəzzən, qəršənne. Komparḏi as sige mənne, komaḥti ann abišoṯe b sariġa w motənne lu bayto.
data.translation: Nach einer Wache sammelt man sie auf, trennt die Rispen ab, tut die Rosinen in einen transportsack für Dinge ohne Halme und bringt sie nach Hause.

rationale: New technical sense and Infectum box; full harvesting sequence identifies the removed and retained material.

summary: New sense 2: (mit m-) die Rispen oder Stiele von Trockenfrüchten abtrennen

data.gloss: (mit m-) die Rispen oder Stiele von Trockenfrüchten abtrennen

rationale: 94/127 has as sige as the removed object, mənne as source, and ann abišoṯe as the resulting raisins. This is material separation, not changing money. One technical attestation, provisionally housed in the present entry.

summary: II Infectum Komparḏi has a generic plural actor, zero-marked removed stalks and an m-marked source. The agricultural context is explicit enough to establish the use without a general figurative bridge from money changing.

The inherited monetary sense and base forms remain untouched. The corpus does not establish that the agricultural verb shares the Kurdish pere dan etymology; provisional sense 2 is not an etymological claim.
Edition spelling 'Nach einer Wache' and lower-case 'transportsack' are preserved as supplied; no translation has been substituted.
Is agricultural mparḏ- a separate homonym from monetary prḏ < Kurdish pere dan, or a related separation use? Check etymology before applying the inherited headword to sense 2.
